title: Mock 6 · Tough Simulator A
blurb: Numericals, close distractors, NOT/EXCEPT items and two 4-question caselets.

questions.q: Which statement about 'alpha' in alternative investments is INCORRECT?
options: Alpha is the return earned purely from bearing systematic market risk
Alpha can arise from bearing unsystematic risk such as illiquidity
Alpha can arise from the superior skill of the fund manager
An alpha of 3%-5% means consistently beating similar-risk assets by that margin per year
questions.explanation: Beta represents systematic risk; alpha is excess return from unsystematic risk (illiquidity, credit quality) and/or manager skill.
hints: Correct (the incorrect statement): return from systematic risk is beta, not alpha.
Wrong choice: this is the first connotation of alpha.
Wrong choice: this is the second connotation of alpha.
Wrong choice: the workbook uses exactly this interpretation.

questions.q: Which statement about migrated Venture Capital Funds is correct as per the workbook?
options: They may launch new schemes under Category II
They were allowed to migrate until July 19, 2027
They cannot launch new schemes, and their existing schemes may be extended up to 2 years with two-thirds approval by value
They are a sub-category of Category III AIF
questions.explanation: Migrated VCFs are not permitted to launch new schemes; extension of existing schemes up to 2 years needs two-thirds of unit holders by value; migration window closed July 19, 2025.
hints: Wrong: migrated VCFs cannot launch new schemes.
Wrong: migration was available till July 19, 2025.
Correct: no new schemes; extension up to 2 years with two-thirds approval.
Wrong: they are a sub-category of VCF under Category I.

questions.q: A Category II AIF scheme has a corpus of ₹400 crore. The estimated expenditure for administration and management over its tenure is ₹40 crore. What is the maximum it can invest in a single investee company?
questions.explanation: Investable funds = corpus net of estimated expenditure for administration and management for the tenure = ₹360 crore; the single-investee limit is 25% = ₹90 crore.
hints: Correct: investable funds = 400 − 40 = 360; 25% × 360 = ₹90 crore.
Wrong: applied 25% to the gross corpus instead of investable funds.
Wrong: 10% figure belongs to the borrowing limit.
Wrong: 50% applies only to LVFs.

questions.q: An angel fund has invested ₹8 crore in total. What is the minimum continuing interest its manager or sponsor must hold?
questions.explanation: For angel funds, continuing interest is not less than 0.5% of the amount invested or ₹50,000, whichever is HIGHER: 0.5% × ₹8 crore = ₹4 lakh.
hints: Wrong: ₹50,000 applies only if 0.5% is lower.
Wrong: 2.5% applies to regular Cat I/II funds.
Wrong: ₹5 crore is the cap for regular Cat I/II funds.
Correct: 0.5% × ₹8 crore = ₹4 lakh, which is higher than ₹50,000.

questions.q: Which of the following applicants qualifies as an Accredited Investor?
options: An individual with annual income ₹1.2 crore and net worth ₹6 crore, of which ₹2 crore is financial assets
An individual with net worth of ₹8 crore, of which ₹4 crore is in financial assets
An individual with annual income of ₹1.8 crore and no other qualifying criterion
A private company with net worth of ₹45 crore
questions.explanation: AI criteria: income ≥ ₹2 crore; or NW ≥ ₹7.5 crore with ≥ ₹3.75 crore financial; or income ≥ ₹1 crore and NW ≥ ₹5 crore with ≥ ₹2.5 crore financial; body corporate NW ≥ ₹50 crore.
hints: Wrong: the combined route needs at least ₹2.5 crore in financial assets.
Correct: meets ₹7.5 crore net worth with at least ₹3.75 crore financial assets.
Wrong: the income-only route needs ₹2 crore.
Wrong: body corporates need net worth of at least ₹50 crore.

questions.q: Which of the following statements about Special Situation Funds is NOT correct?
options: Each SSF scheme must have a minimum corpus of ₹100 crore
Minimum investment by an accredited investor in an SSF is ₹5 crore
Stressed loans acquired by an SSF are subject to a minimum lock-in of 6 months
An SSF may accept investment from any Category II AIF
questions.explanation: The special situation fund shall not accept investments from any other AIF other than a special situation fund.
hints: Wrong choice: ₹100 crore minimum corpus is correct.
Wrong choice: ₹5 crore for AIs (₹10 crore otherwise) is correct.
Wrong choice: 6-month lock-in is correct (not applicable on recovery).
Correct (the incorrect statement): an SSF accepts investment from no other AIF except another SSF.

questions.q: Which statement about downstream investment by a Category I/II AIF is correct under FEMA/NDI Rules?
options: It is treated as foreign investment whenever more than 10% of the corpus is from non-residents
It is always treated as domestic investment because AIFs are SEBI-registered
It is foreign investment only if the custodian is foreign
It is treated as indirect foreign investment if the sponsor or manager is not Indian owned and controlled, irrespective of the extent of foreign money in the corpus
questions.explanation: Downstream investment is indirect foreign investment if either the sponsor or the manager is not Indian owned and controlled; the extent of foreign investment in the corpus is not a factor.
hints: Wrong: extent of foreign investment in the corpus is not a factor.
Wrong: SEBI registration does not make it domestic.
Wrong: the custodian is irrelevant.
Correct: ownership/control of sponsor and manager decides; corpus composition is not a factor.

questions.q: Consider: (i) A trust cannot sue or be sued in its own name. (ii) In an LLP, a partner is jointly liable for another partner's negligence. (iii) A company AIF is restricted to private placement to 200 investors. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: A trust is represented by its trustee; in an LLP no partner is liable for another's misconduct or negligence; companies are restricted to 200 investors in private placements.
hints: Correct: the trustee sues on its behalf; companies are limited to 200 in private placement.
Wrong: (ii) is false as there is no joint liability in an LLP.
Wrong: (ii) is false.
Wrong: (ii) is false.

questions.q: Which structure has TWO pooling vehicles and routes ALL foreign money through the domestic SEBI-registered AIF, with only AIF Regulations applicable?
questions.explanation: Per Table 5.1, the unified structure has 2 pooling vehicles, AIF Regulations apply, and the domestic AIF invests in investee companies.
hints: Wrong: parallel has two vehicles but the offshore fund invests directly under FVCI/FDI.
Wrong: one vehicle under FVCI regulations.
Wrong: one vehicle and only domestic investors.
Correct: two vehicles, offshore fund feeds the domestic AIF.

questions.q: A debenture pays a 12% annual coupon in monthly instalments. Its effective annual yield is closest to:
hints: Wrong: ignores compounding.
Wrong: that is quarterly compounding.
Wrong: arithmetic error.

questions.q: A CTR is received by the trustee on April 25. The trustee sends observations on May 20. What is the latest date for the manager to submit its reply?
questions.explanation: Within 15 days from receipt of the trustee/sponsor observations, the manager shall make changes and reply; May 20 + 15 days = June 4.
hints: Correct: within 15 days of receipt of observations (May 20 + 15 days).
Wrong: applied 30 days.
Wrong: applied 5 days.
Wrong: no such timeline.

questions.q: Which statement about SEBI's performance benchmarking guidelines is INCORRECT?
options: Data for March 31 shall be audited, while September 30 data may be unaudited
Benchmarking is carried out on post-tax NAV of the scheme
Performance data and benchmarks are reported in both INR and USD
Customised reports are called 'Performance Report', not 'Benchmark Report'
questions.explanation: The performance reporting and benchmarking shall be carried out on pre-tax NAV of the scheme.
hints: Wrong choice: this is correct.
Correct (the incorrect statement): benchmarking is on pre-tax NAV.
Wrong choice: this is correct.
Wrong choice: this is correct.

questions.q: Two senior partners handle commitments and investor relationships, while two junior partners oversee fund management. In key-man terms, the senior partners are best described as:
questions.explanation: Concepts of 'super key person' and 'standard key person' are used; senior partners responsible for commitments and investor relationships can be super key persons.
hints: Wrong: the junior partners are standard key persons.
Wrong: an LLP compliance role, not a key-man concept.
Correct: the workbook illustrates exactly this split.
Wrong: unrelated to key-man clause.

questions.q: An association of AIFs may notify benchmarking agencies only if it represents, in terms of membership, at least what share of AIFs?
questions.explanation: Any association of AIFs which represents at least 33% of the number of AIFs may notify one or more benchmarking agencies.
hints: Wrong: the test is by number, not AUM.
Correct: at least 33% of the number of AIFs.
Wrong: wrong threshold.
Wrong: wrong threshold.

questions.q: Audit of which of the following PPM sections is MANDATORY (not optional) in the annual PPM audit?
options: Distribution of proceeds and additional return charged to investors
questions.explanation: Audit of 'Risk Factors', 'Legal, Regulatory and Tax Considerations', 'Track Record of First Time Managers', fee illustration and glossary is optional; distributions and additional return are within mandatory scope.
hints: Wrong: risk factors audit is optional.
Wrong: legal/regulatory/tax audit is optional.
Wrong: glossary audit is optional.
Correct: review of distributions and additional return is part of the audit scope.

questions.q: An AIF wants each investor to waive the SEBI PPM template and annual PPM audit. What minimum commitment must each investor make for this exemption (non-LVF route)?
questions.explanation: AIFs where each investor commits at least ₹70 crore (USD 10 million) and provides a waiver are exempt from the template and PPM audit requirement.
hints: Correct: ₹70 crore/USD 10 million plus a waiver.
Wrong: ₹25 crore defines an LVF.
Wrong: ₹100 crore relates to angel fund audit threshold.
Wrong: not the threshold.

questions.q: On a change of manager, two independent valuers value a dissenting investor's units at ₹240 crore and ₹260 crore. The buy-out must be at not less than:
questions.explanation: Exit shall be at a value not less than the average of the two independent valuations: (240 + 260) ÷ 2 = ₹250 crore.
hints: Wrong: the lower valuation is not the floor.
Wrong: the higher valuation is not required.
Correct: not less than the average of the two valuations.
Wrong: sum, not average.

questions.q: Which statement about winding up and liquidation of an AIF scheme is correct?
options: The liquidation period is 3 years after expiry of tenure
No AIF may launch a new Liquidation Scheme after April 25, 2024
Dissolution period can be entered with approval of two-thirds of investors
Unsold assets after the dissolution period may be held indefinitely
questions.explanation: No new liquidation schemes post April 25, 2024; liquidation period is 1 year; dissolution needs 75% approval; unsold investments after dissolution are mandatorily distributed in specie.
hints: Wrong: liquidation period is 1 year.
Correct: SEBI barred new liquidation schemes post April 25, 2024.
Wrong: needs at least 75% of investors by value.
Wrong: they must be mandatorily distributed in specie.

questions.q: A bond of face value ₹1,000 pays an 8% annual coupon and matures in 2 years. If the required return is 10%, its value is closest to:
questions.explanation: Value = I × PVA + F × PV = 80/1.1 + 1080/1.1² = ₹965.29. Coupon below required return means a discount to par.
hints: Wrong: true only when coupon equals required return.
Wrong: a premium arises only when coupon exceeds required return.
Wrong: ignored the first coupon.

questions.q: Next year's free cash flow of a company is forecast at ₹220 crore. If WACC is 13% and the long-term growth rate is 5%, the terminal value is:
questions.explanation: Terminal value = FCF(T+1) ÷ (WACC − g) = 220 ÷ 0.08 = ₹2,750 crore.
hints: Wrong: divided by WACC only.
Wrong: divided by growth only.
Wrong: divided by WACC + g.

questions.q: An offshore feeder entity holds Indian assets worth ₹15 crore, which constitute 40% of its total assets. Under the indirect transfer provisions, its shares:
options: Derive value substantially from India, since Indian assets exceed ₹10 crore
Do not derive value substantially from India, since the 50% test is not met
Derive value substantially from India because any Indian asset suffices
Are always exempt because the investor is non-resident
questions.explanation: Value is derived substantially from India only if Indian assets exceed ₹10 crore AND represent at least 50% of all assets; 40% fails the second test.
hints: Wrong: the ₹10 crore test alone is not enough.
Correct: both conditions (> ₹10 crore AND ≥ 50%) must be satisfied.
Wrong: thresholds apply.
Wrong: non-residents can be taxed under indirect transfer.

questions.q: Which situation represents a conflict of interest that the workbook says a distributor should avoid?
options: Comparing the scheme with a similar, comparable AIF using adequate information
Explaining to the investor that past performance is no guarantee
Obtaining a capital commitment from a company in which the distributor holds 12% of paid-up capital
Using its own staff to perform In-Person Verification
questions.explanation: Distributors should avoid capital commitments from affiliates or entities where the distributor is a director or holds more than 10% of paid-up capital (related party concern).
hints: Wrong: comparisons with comparable AIFs are allowed.
Wrong: appropriate risk disclosure.
Correct: commitments from entities where the distributor is a director or holds more than 10% should be avoided.
Wrong: a recommended good practice.

questions.q: Based on the case, what is the scheme's PIC multiple?
questions.explanation: PIC multiple = paid-in capital ÷ commitments = 900 ÷ 1,000 = 0.90; the fund is near the end of drawdown.
hints: Wrong: that is DPI.
Wrong: inverse ratio.
Wrong: arithmetic error.
questions.case: Sahyadri Growth Fund II, a Category II AIF scheme, has total capital commitments of ₹1,000 crore. By the end of Year 5 the manager has drawn down ₹900 crore from investors. Cumulative cash distributions to investors so far are ₹540 crore, and the independent valuer has estimated the fair value of the remaining (unrealised) portfolio at ₹810 crore. An investor asks his distributor to explain how the fund is doing using the standard private-fund multiples.

questions.q: What is the scheme's DPI?
questions.explanation: DPI = cumulative distributions ÷ PIC = 540 ÷ 900 = 0.60.
hints: Wrong: divided by commitments instead of paid-in capital.
Wrong: that is RVPI (and PIC).
Wrong: that is TVPI.

Cumulative cash distributions to investors so far are ₹540 crore, and the independent valuer has estimated the fair value of the remaining (unrealised) portfolio at ₹810 crore. An investor asks his distributor to explain how the fund is doing using the standard private-fund multiples.

questions.q: What is the scheme's TVPI?
questions.explanation: TVPI = (distributions + residual value) ÷ PIC = 1,350 ÷ 900 = 1.50 = DPI 0.60 + RVPI 0.90.
hints: Wrong: divided by commitments.
Wrong: that is RVPI.
Wrong: arithmetic error.

questions.q: Later the fund draws the full ₹1,000 crore, exits every investment and total distributions reach ₹1,620 crore. Which statement is correct at that point?
options: DPI = 1.62 but TVPI = 2.43 because RVPI remains
TVPI = 1.62 but DPI = 0 because the fund has closed
MOIC will be lower than TVPI because all capital calls are met
questions.explanation: When the fund has fully exited, the RVPI is reduced to zero and DPI = TVPI (1,620 ÷ 1,000 = 1.62); MOIC equals TVPI when all capital calls are met.
hints: Wrong: no unrealised value remains.
Correct: at full realisation RVPI is zero and DPI equals TVPI.
Wrong: DPI captures all distributions.
Wrong: once all calls are met, MOIC equals TVPI.

questions.q: Based on the case, how much will the manager receive as catch-up?
questions.explanation: Catch-up = 25% of (distributable cash − investors' capital and hurdle) = 0.25 × 400 = ₹100 crore.
hints: Wrong: 25% of the full ₹900 crore.
Wrong: 20% of ₹400 crore.
Wrong: that is the carried interest.
questions.case: In its final year, Kaveri Credit Opportunities Fund (Category II) has ₹900 crore available for distribution after all fees, expenses and taxes. Investors are still owed ₹500 crore to receive back their contributed capital plus the 10% preferred return. The PPM provides a European waterfall: (1) capital and hurdle to investors, (2) a catch-up to the manager of 25% of the balance remaining after step 1, and (3) the residual split 80% to investors and 20% to the manager as carried interest.

questions.q: How much will the manager receive as carried interest after the catch-up?
questions.explanation: Residual after catch-up = 400 − 100 = ₹300 crore; carry = 20% × 300 = ₹60 crore.
hints: Wrong: 20% of ₹400 crore ignores catch-up.
Wrong: that is the catch-up.
Wrong: 20% of ₹900 crore.

questions.q: What is the total distribution to investors in the final year?
questions.explanation: Investors receive ₹500 crore (capital + hurdle) plus 80% of the ₹300 crore residual (₹240 crore) = ₹740 crore.
hints: Wrong: applied 80% to the full ₹400 crore without catch-up.
Wrong: arithmetic error.
Wrong: ignores the residual share.

questions.q: If an earlier deal-by-deal payout had overpaid the manager, which clause would let investors recover the excess at the end of the fund?
questions.explanation: Clawback entitles investors to reverse incentive fees taken during the fund's life so that fees reflect a full netting of profits and losses over its life.
hints: Correct: clawback reverses excess incentive fees after netting profits and losses.
Wrong: catch-up benefits the manager.
Wrong: used mainly in hedge funds to avoid repeat fees.
Wrong: MFN equalises investor terms.
